title: Tamil Nadu circa 1900 — SCALE Framework

period.historical_context: Tamil-speaking regions of the Madras Presidency, under British colonial rule
period.setting_type: A historically inspired South Indian town street with nearby village life

Subject.description: Everyday Tamil people in the year 1900: men wearing traditional veshti and angavastram, women wearing handwoven cotton sarees, children in simple traditional clothing, a vegetable seller, a potter, and a bullock-cart driver.
details: Natural, historically plausible faces and clothing
Handwoven cotton fabrics in muted earthy colours
No modern hairstyles, accessories, or synthetic-looking fabrics

Composition.camera_view: Wide cinematic establishing shot at human eye level
Composition.framing: A lively street scene with people in the foreground, tiled-roof houses and small shops in the middle ground, and a South Indian temple gopuram in the distant background
visual_layers: Foreground: a woman carrying a brass water pot and a street vendor arranging vegetables
Middle ground: pedestrians, a bullock cart, a tea or provisions shop, and traditional houses
Background: temple architecture, palm trees, and a hazy rural skyline
Composition.depth: Natural atmospheric depth, realistic scale, documentary-style framing

Action.description: A normal morning in Tamil Nadu around 1900. People walk along the dusty street, a vendor sells fresh produce, a potter carries clay vessels, a bullock cart moves slowly, and neighbours converse outside their homes.
motion_details: Bullocks walk at a calm pace
People move naturally without looking at the camera
A woman adjusts the brass pot as she walks

Location.description: A traditional Tamil town street in the Madras Presidency, circa 1900
environment: Palm trees and a dusty unpaved street
historical_guardrails: Do not depict modern Tamil Nadu state symbols or post-1947 Indian national flags
Avoid modern roads, vehicles, electric streetlights, concrete high-rises, mobile phones, and plastic items
Avoid presenting contemporary Chennai landmarks as they appear today

Esthetic.style: Photorealistic historical reconstruction with the feel of an early 20th-century documentary photograph brought to life
Esthetic.lighting: Soft golden early-morning sunlight with gentle atmospheric haze
Esthetic.texture: Subtle film grain, natural skin and fabric texture, weathered lime plaster, aged wood, and dusty ground
Esthetic.mood: Authentic, calm, culturally rich, dignified, and observational

generation_prompt: Create a historically inspired, photorealistic cinematic scene of Tamil Nadu around the year 1900, in the Tamil-speaking region of the Madras Presidency. Show an ordinary morning on a traditional town street: Tamil men in veshti and angavastram, women in handwoven cotton sarees, children, a vegetable seller, a potter, and a slowly moving bullock cart. Compose the scene as a wide eye-level establishing shot, with people and vendors in the foreground, lime-washed tiled-roof houses and small shops in the middle ground, and a traditional Dravidian temple gopuram with palm trees in the distance. Use soft golden morning light, dusty earth, brass and clay vessels, muted terracotta and indigo tones, realistic historical details, and subtle early-photography texture. The scene should feel like an authentic everyday moment, not a royal or fantasy depiction. Exclude modern vehicles, plastic, electric streetlights, mobile phones, concrete high-rises, contemporary clothing, and post-1947 national symbols.
negative_prompt: Modern cars, buses, motorcycles, bicycles with modern styling
Electric streetlights, power lines, mobile phones, plastic objects
Modern concrete buildings, glass towers, paved highways
Contemporary fashion, synthetic fabrics, modern footwear
Post-1947 Indian national flags or modern state emblems
Fantasy costumes, exaggerated temple architecture, tourist-postcard styling
Modern Chennai skyline or present-day landmarks

recommended_output.historical_accuracy_note: This is a representative creative reconstruction, not a claim that every Tamil region looked identical in 1900. Clothing, architecture, and daily life varied by community, occupation, wealth, and locality.
